subject: Azure Partner Center: seller collaboration + intake workback for Aventis
messages:
From: John Doe <john.doe@aventis.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Suresh <priya.suresh@aventis.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Partner Center intake — Aventis account mapping

Hi Hannah / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — Aventis is excited about the prospect of moving some of our inference workloads to Redwood. Before we lock the co-sell registration I wanted to confirm a couple of operational items so our field sellers and procurement teams are aligned: 

- Can you share the suggested seller mapping approach for our account list (we have multiple business units in scope)?
- What artifacts do your Azure reps need to accept a Partner Center referral (SOW, SKU mapping, MPN info)?
- Any timing expectations for co-sell registration approval and marketplace listing sync?

I've attached our current account roster (aventis_account_map.xlsx) for reference. Happy to jump on a short call Monday if helpful.

Best,
John
Director, Cloud Architecture
Aventis Health

[attachment: aventis_account_map.xlsx (spreadsheet, 87KB)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@aventis.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Partner Center intake — Aventis account mapping

John — appreciate the roster and great questions. High level answers below, plus a short proposed workback so our field sellers can act without ambiguity.

Quick answers:
- Seller mapping: we recommend an ownership token approach (primary seller + 1 backup) per global account and per major BU. For partners like Aventis with multi-BU footprints, we map at the pillar level to avoid split leads. I opened the attached intake playbook (pc-intake-playbook-v1.pdf) which includes the mapping template.
- Required artifacts for referral acceptance: MPN/partner ID, a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) doc, and the target SKU list for co-sell registration. Legal SOWs rarely needed upfront unless procurement requires them.
- Timing: partner intake -> co-sell registration typically 5–10 business days if seller consent is in place. Marketplace listing sync can run in parallel but expect 2–3 weeks for full marketplace publishing depending on SKU approvals.

Proposed immediate workback (week 1):
1) Internal mapping review (Redwood) — Hannah/Vanessa/Karthik — 2 business days
2) Send seller assignments to Aventis and get seller consent — John/Priya — 3 business days
3) Formal MAP + MPN collection — mutual — 3 business days
4) Submit Partner Center referral & co-sell registration — Redwood/Avnetis — submit day 7

Ask: Vanessa/Karthik/Ben, can you take the internal mapping pass on the attached spreadsheet and return annotated ownership tokens by EOD Thursday? I'll then send to John/Priya for consent.

Happy to run a 30-min alignment tomorrow 9:30am PT if that's easier — John, Priya, does that work?

Thanks,
Hannah
Head of Field Partnerships 
Redwood Inference

[attachment: pc-intake-playbook-v1.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Partner Center intake — Aventis account mapping

Looping in these notes after a quick pass on the spreadsheet. Key decisions and edge cases: 

- Multi-BU accounts: flagged Aventis-Clinical and Aventis-Claims to be split and assigned to different seller pockets — see rows colored yellow.
- Regional ownership: some EU-heavy accounts are shared with the EMEA seller team; we should mark them as shared to avoid duplicate opportunities in Partner Center.
- Orphans: three accounts had no recent owner in our CRM; Ben, can you reach out to Sales Ops to identify the right rep or mark as "ask-field"?

I've left inline comments in aventis_account_map.xlsx and set proposed owners. If we keep the primary+backup token model, mapping should be fast. Also propose we capture the expected annual ARR band per account in the spreadsheet to prioritize co-sell registration order.

If we can finalize internal tokens by Friday EOD we'll be on track for a submission the week of Dec 13.

Vanessa
Sr. Partner Manager, Redwood Inference

From: John Doe <john.doe@aventis.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Suresh <priya.suresh@aventis.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Partner Center intake — Aventis account mapping

Thanks everyone — the proposed cadence looks good.

Priya and I will confirm seller consent on our side by Friday and return the MAP + MPN details. For the orphan accounts, Ben if you can ping Sales Ops that would be great; otherwise we'll nominate internal AMs.

One operational ask: when you submit the Partner Center referral, can Redwood include a short summary field that lists the shortlist of SKUs we're targeting for co-sell? That makes approval faster on our side.

See you on the 30-min sync if we need it — otherwise we'll proceed with the consent loop.

Best,
John
Director, Cloud Architecture
Aventis Health
